summary: Sawan Singh's replies to Western initiates between 1919 and 1948, many of them troubleshooting. To those who see nothing he says to keep the attention on the darkness in the focus of the eyes and 'peep' into it while repeating the five names: the darkness will change into light. He gives time splits (three-quarters repetition, one-quarter listening; lengthen one hour to two), says breathing is to be left alone and no force applied to the spine, and treats numbness of the limbs as the sign that withdrawal is working. He describes the expected sequence (sparks and fleeting flashes, sky and stars, one large white star to be fixed upon until it 'bursts', then sun and moon, then the Master's radiant form), explains intermittent stars as lack of concentration and a 'shaky mind', and warns against accepting anything offered by inner figures or telling others one's visions.
why_relevant: Direct written troubleshooting for initiates who see darkness, flashes or stars; one of the clearest statements in the lineage of what to do when nothing is seen.

date_evidence.basis: Letters written before the author's death in 1948 (foreword in saved text). The saved OCR prints no edition year; archive.org lending copy bwb_KU-749-842 of the same title is catalogued as 1965, and item huzurmaharajsawansinghspiritualgems is catalogued 1948. 1965 is given as the latest year a printed edition is attested in the archive metadata I saw; the first-edition year (c. 1958) is from memory, not verified.

notes: In copyright (RSSB). Saved file is excerpts only: 81 context windows, about 13% of the OCR text, selected by keyword (flash, star, darkness, peep, sparks, candle, blue, sun and moon, etc.). Reading agent: paraphrase + anchor only. The 'candlelight' instruction (p. 300-301) is ambiguous between an imagined flame and darkness as support; record as the source words it.
